cities.base: Central Siem Reap, close to the old market and pub street, walkable to restaurants and within a short tuk tuk of all temple routes.
cities.name: Siem Reap

cities.base: Old French quarter near the riverside, walkable to the market and colonial-era shopfronts.
cities.name: Battambang

places.name: Angkor Wat
places.note: Go for the 5am gate open, the causeway crowd by full sunrise is the thing to avoid, not the temple itself.

places.name: Beng Mealea
places.note: Unrestored and half-collapsed, better than Ta Prohm if you only get to pick one. A $10 single ticket is sold on site (2026); check the price if you hold an Angkor pass.

places.name: Koh Ker pyramid temple
places.note: Almost nobody here, and the pyramid form is unlike anything else at Angkor. The 1, 3 and 7-day Angkor passes are not stated to cover it, so check the price.

places.name: Kompong Phluk floating village boat
places.note: A working fishing village, not a show, ask for a guide who slows down and lets you land.

places.name: Phnom Sampeau killing caves and bat exodus
places.note: Khmer Rouge-era killing caves with a memorial to the victims, sobering rather than scenic, then the bat exodus at about 17:30 to 18:15. Free per the 2026 listing; arrive by 17:30 to get a spot.

places.name: Old French Quarter
places.note: Grid of shophouse streets near the river, colonial-era facades in varying states of repair, quiet enough to wander without a map. No single building is the sight, the walk is.

places.name: Phare, The Cambodian Circus
places.note: Theater and acrobatics, not a real circus: about an hour nightly at 20:00, plus 17:00 matinees Wed, Fri and Sun from November 2026 to March 2027. Seats $38, $28 or $18 (2026), book ahead.

places.name: Bamboo Train (Norry), O Dambong
places.note: 20 minutes each way on a bamboo platform over a rickety line, fun for ten minutes and now a tourist track with stalls at the turnaround. Runs 07:30 to 17:30 daily; visitors report $5 shared or $10 private, so check the price.

places.name: Psar Nat (Central Market)
places.note: Art deco covered market from the 1930s, gold stalls, produce, dry goods. Busiest and coolest before 9am, quieter by midday.

places.name: Sangkae Riverside
places.note: Paved path along the river, locals doing evening exercise, a few food carts setting up. Low-key, good for the unhurried second evening rather than a destination in itself.

places.name: Wat Banan
places.note: An 11th-century hilltop temple with five towers, about 350 steps up. Called Angkor Wat's little sibling, which oversells it, but the climb and the view over rice paddies earn an hour if there is time.

places.name: Phare Ponleu Selpak
places.note: The arts school that later spawned Phare, The Cambodian Circus in Siem Reap. Performances here are occasional, so check the schedule and the price before counting on one.

places.name: Battambang Museum
places.note: Small provincial museum of Angkor-era sandstone carvings from the surrounding temples, a fine rain-day hour. Free with donations welcome; it closes for lunch, hours vary, check.

places.name: Wat Kor Village (heritage houses)
places.note: A handful of century-old wooden houses, one open for tours. Interesting if wooden Khmer architecture is a specific interest, otherwise a long tuk tuk detour for not much, skip in favor of the old French quarter walk which covers similar ground with less effort.

places.name: Nary Kitchen Cooking Class
places.note: Market walk followed by a hands-on class in a home kitchen, small groups. A good rainy-day or slow-second-day option if the traveler wants something active beyond walking, though it eats half the day.

places.name: Kinyei
places.note: Small specialty coffee shop, one of the first in Battambang to roast its own beans. Good spot to sit before the market walk, not a sight but a reliable break.

places.name: Lan Chan Restaurant
places.note: Riverside restaurant serving Khmer standards, amok, lok lak, fresh fish from the Sangkae. Straightforward, no theatrics, good spot to end the second evening before or after the riverside walk.

places.name: South Gate of Angkor Thom
places.note: The causeway with the gods and demons pulling the naga, best preserved of the five gates, everyone photographs the giant faces on the tower above it but the tuk tuk queue behind it moves slowly around 9am.

places.name: Bayon
places.note: 216 stone faces looking out from 54 towers, covered by the general Angkor pass, climb to the upper terrace for the closest views, crowds build fast after 9am so pair it right after Angkor Wat sunrise.

places.name: Baphuon
places.note: Three tiered pyramid temple a short walk from Bayon, the long raised causeway is the best part, much quieter than Bayon itself since most tour groups skip it.

places.name: Phimeanakas
places.note: Small steep pyramid inside the Royal Palace enclosure, the climb is short and the stone is worn smooth, skip if you are pressed for time since it adds little beyond what Baphuon already shows.

places.name: Terrace of the Elephants
places.note: 350 meter reviewing wall carved with elephants and garudas, faces the old royal square, walk its full length rather than photographing the near end and moving on.

places.name: Terrace of the Leper King
places.note: Right next to the Elephant Terrace, the carved inner wall in the narrow trench behind the platform is the actual reason to stop, easy to miss if you only glance at the front.

places.name: North Gate of Angkor Thom
places.note: Same face towers as the South Gate but almost no one stops here, useful if the South Gate crowd is bad and you just want the photo without the wait.

places.name: Prasat Chrung (corner shrine)
places.note: One of four small corner shrines marking the city walls, only worth a stop if you are already passing it. Covered by the Angkor pass (1-day $37, 3-day $62, 7-day $72, 2026), no charge on top.

places.name: Food stalls near Bayon car park
places.note: Simple noodle and rice stalls where drivers and guides eat, fine for a fast lunch between temples, not a destination in itself, don't expect much beyond fried rice and cold drinks.

places.name: South Gate causeway viewpoint
places.note: Stand back from the gate itself to get the full tower with faces and the row of stone giants in one frame, arrive before 8am for a clear shot without a line of tuk tuks in it.

places.name: Angkor Thom city wall and moat walk
places.note: The laterite walls and wide moat ringing the old city are visible from the road in, worth a slow look from the van window or a short stop, not something to build time around.

places.name: Add-on tours to nearby villages from Angkor Thom drivers
places.note: Skip. Drivers sometimes pitch a village or workshop stop on the way out, these are usually commission stops for shops, they eat into the time you need to get back before the afternoon heat and crowds elsewhere.

places.name: Ta Prohm Temple
places.note: Strangler fig and silk-cotton roots over the stonework, and the Tomb Raider link draws a crowd fast; arrive at opening, because by 10am the root shots are people, not trees. Covered by the Angkor pass (1-day $37, 3-day $62, 7-day $72, 2026), no charge on top.

places.name: Hall of Dancers, Ta Prohm
places.note: A carved gallery near the east entrance with apsara reliefs on some columns, quieter than the root courtyards since most people head for the famous tree first. Covered by the Angkor pass (1-day $37, 3-day $62, 7-day $72, 2026), no charge on top.

places.name: Ta Prohm East Gate
places.note: Entering from the east instead of the main west gate means walking against the tour group flow, a quieter approach to the same ruins if your driver drops you there. Covered by the Angkor pass (1-day $37, 3-day $62, 7-day $72, 2026), no charge on top.

places.name: Banteay Kdei
places.note: Buddhist monastic temple with the same jungle-reclaimed feel as Ta Prohm and far fewer visitors, the quiet counterpoint after Ta Prohm. Covered by the Angkor pass (1-day $37, 3-day $62, 7-day $72, 2026), no charge on top.

places.name: Sras Srang
places.note: Royal bathing pool across from Banteay Kdei with a sandstone landing terrace, a 20 minute stop by day and a quiet sunset option instead of the Angkor Wat causeway. Covered by the Angkor pass (1-day $37, 3-day $62, 7-day $72, 2026), no charge on top.

places.name: Preah Khan
places.note: Large flat temple complex with long causeways and garuda-holding-naga balustrades, part jungle-reclaimed like Ta Prohm but bigger and less packed; allow an hour. Covered by the Angkor pass (1-day $37, 3-day $62, 7-day $72, 2026), no charge on top.

places.name: Neak Pean
places.note: Small island temple in an artificial pond, reached by a walkway over the water, a quick add on the Preah Khan side of the loop. Covered by the Angkor pass (1-day $37, 3-day $62, 7-day $72, 2026), no charge on top.

places.name: Ta Som
places.note: Small temple with a tree-engulfed east gate in the spirit of Ta Prohm but almost empty, an easy add if the loop has time. Covered by the Angkor pass (1-day $37, 3-day $62, 7-day $72, 2026), no charge on top.

places.name: Local restaurants near Ta Prohm parking area
places.note: A cluster of simple open-air stalls and restaurants near the temple parking lots serve fried noodles, lok lak, and cold drinks. Nothing memorable, just functional and air conditioned enough to reset before the afternoon temples.

places.name: Angkor National Museum
places.note: Khmer sculpture overview in town, best before the temples or on a rain day; the Gallery of a Thousand Buddhas is the room not to miss. Open daily 08:30 to 18:30, one visitor paid $12 plus $5 for the audio guide, so check the price.

places.name: Cuisine Wat Damnak
places.note: Chef Joannes Riviere's seasonal Khmer tasting menu, 5 or 6 courses for $30 to $40 (2026). Book ahead; closed Sunday per the current listing, an older one said Monday, so confirm.

places.name: Mahob Khmer Cuisine
places.note: Modern Khmer, a la carte mains $15 to $22 or the weekly tasting menu at $45 (2026).

places.name: The Sugar Palm
places.note: Khmer home cooking; order the fish amok, $9 (2026). Dinner only, and listed as closed Monday, so confirm.

places.name: Marum
places.note: Social-enterprise training restaurant serving Khmer tapas at $5 to $9 a plate (2026), so order two or three. Dinner only, closed Sunday.

places.name: Khmer Kitchen
places.note: Cheap, busy tourist standard by the Old Market: fish amok $5, beef lok lak $4 (2026). Fine for a fast lunch, not a destination.

places.name: Banlle Vegetarian
places.note: Plant-based Khmer plates at $4 to $8 (2026). Shut 14:00 to 17:00 between lunch and dinner, and closed Tuesday.

places.name: Embassy by Chef Kimsan
places.note: Tasting menu that changes monthly, $55 to $75 (2026) with a wine pairing on offer; the splurge night of the trip.

places.name: Malis
places.note: Khmer restaurant with a large garden, best for the $9 free-flow breakfast (2025) after a sunrise start. No dinner price found, so check the price for a main.

places.name: Cambodia Landmine Museum
places.note: Non-profit museum founded by Aki Ra, a former child soldier turned deminer. $7, under 13 free (2026), open daily 07:30 to 17:30; pair it with Banteay Srei on the same road.

places.name: War Museum Cambodia
places.note: Open-air yard of rusted tanks, aircraft and artillery from the civil war years. About $5 per a visitor report, so check the price; open daily 08:00 to 17:30.

places.name: Wat Preah Prom Rath
places.note: Working pagoda in the centre with murals of the life of the Buddha, a gold Buddha and gardens. Open 07:00 to 18:00; check the price, cover shoulders and knees.

places.name: Wat Bo
places.note: Pagoda known for its 19th-century wall paintings, the oldest murals in town. Free entrance; hours vary, check.

places.name: Wat Damnak
places.note: Pagoda with carved stonework, lily ponds, a school and a library, quieter than the central wats. Check the price; hours vary, check.

places.name: Wat Thmei memorial stupa
places.note: Glass-walled stupa holding the bones of Khmer Rouge victims, a short and sobering stop on the way to the temples. Check the price; hours vary, check.

places.name: Preah Ang Chek Preah Ang Chorm Shrine
places.note: Shrine to two venerated statues where locals come to pray, open from early morning to 17:00. Free; go early to see it in use.

places.name: Royal Independence Gardens
places.note: Independence-era park from the 1950s, open round the clock and free. Come at dusk for the fruit bat colony leaving the trees and the lit bridges.

places.name: Old Market (Psar Chas)
places.note: Produce, textiles and food stalls under one roof, free to wander 07:00 to 21:00. The produce side is busiest early.

places.name: Siem Reap Art Center Night Market
places.note: Crafts, snacks and Apsara dance shows, free to enter, 16:00 to 23:00, closed Sunday per one listing. Not the same place as the Angkor Night Market.

places.name: Artisans Angkor (Living Arts Village)
places.note: Workshops where young Cambodians learn stone carving and silk work, open 07:30 to 18:00. Free to walk round per a visitor report, so check the price.

places.name: APOPO Visitor Center
places.note: Trained rats that sniff out landmines, with a live demo; about $10 for the tour, open 08:30 to 16:30. A good pair with the Landmine Museum.

places.name: Pre Rup
places.note: 10th-century temple mountain and the sunset climb on the east side of the park, open 06:00 to 19:00. Covered by the Angkor pass (1-day $37, 3-day $62, 7-day $72, 2026), no charge on top.

places.name: East Mebon
places.note: Dedicated in 953 on an island in the now dry East Baray; do not miss the large stone elephants at the corners. Covered by the Angkor pass (1-day $37, 3-day $62, 7-day $72, 2026), no charge on top.

places.name: Bakong (Roluos group)
places.note: Built in 881, the first sandstone temple mountain, elephants on the lower tiers; Preah Ko (879) and Lolei (893) are minutes away. Pass covers it, no charge on top; hours vary, check.

places.name: Banteay Srei
places.note: Consecrated in 967 and built by courtiers, not a king, with the finest red sandstone carving at Angkor. Entry only with the Angkor pass, no charge on top; hours vary, check.

places.name: Phnom Krom
places.note: Hilltop temple on a 140 m hill above the Tonle Sap, open 06:00 to 19:00, best for the late light over the lake. Covered by the Angkor pass (1-day $37, 3-day $62, 7-day $72, 2026), no charge on top.

places.name: West Baray
places.note: Angkorian reservoir 7.8 by 2.1 km, with the West Mebon on its island; locals swim and take boats out. Check the price for a boat; hours vary, check.

places.name: Chong Kneas floating village
places.note: Floating village on the Tonle Sap reached by boat, the closest of the lake villages to town. No boat price found, so check the price; hours vary, check.

places.name: Jaan Bai
places.note: Upscale Khmer from local ingredients, built for sharing; the 6-dish set is $21.50 a head (2026). The best dinner in town.

places.name: Smokin' Pot
places.note: Restaurant and cooking school, most meals about $5 (2026). Easy lunch near the river.

places.name: Nary Kitchen
places.note: Family restaurant and cooking school; order the fish amok, most dishes $3 or less on an undated price list, so check the price.

outings.why: The sunrise causeway is a crowd not a view unless you're there at 5am, but the Bayon faces afterward are worth the early pickup.
outings.name: Angkor Wat sunrise + Angkor Thom + Bayon
outings.fallback: Sleep in and do the Ta Prohm/Preah Khan loop instead, temples are still open midday.

outings.why: The tree-root temple gets swarmed by 10am so it has to go first, then two quieter stops round out the day with a lunch break.
outings.name: Ta Prohm, Preah Khan, Banteay Kdei loop
outings.fallback: Shorten to just Ta Prohm and rest through the heat of the day.

outings.why: Unrestored, half-collapsed jungle temples with almost nobody there, but it's 2-2.5 hours each way on dirt road and not worth doing tired.
outings.name: Beng Mealea and Koh Ker remote temple day
outings.season: dry season easiest on the road, Nov-Feb
outings.fallback: Skip the day entirely and add a slower morning in Siem Reap instead, it's genuinely optional.

outings.why: A real fishing village on stilts, morning light is best, and the trip lives or dies on whether the guide slows down and lets you land instead of running a human safari.
outings.name: Tonle Sap floating village boat trip, Kompong Phluk
outings.season: year-round, better in wet season when water is high
outings.fallback: None needed, it's a half day and rarely cancelled.

outings.why: The norry is a fun 20-minute tourist-track ride now, and Phnom Sampeau's caves and dusk bat swarm are the more affecting half of the afternoon.
outings.name: Bamboo train (norry) and Phnom Sampeau killing caves + bat exodus
outings.fallback: If it rains, the caves are still open, just skip the bats.

outings.why: An unhurried walk through colonial shopfronts and the market, riverside is the move at dusk.
outings.name: Battambang old French quarter, market, riverside
outings.fallback: None needed, it's low-key by design.

destination.name: Cambodia
destination.pitch: Eight days for Angkor done properly plus two nights of slower, non-temple Battambang, not a third city bolted on.
destination.caveat: Everyone connects through Seoul, Bangkok, or Singapore, so total travel time from the US eats a day and a half of the trip each way, and the remote temple day is a long van ride for anyone who doesn't love ruins. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.food: Battambang's old French quarter and riverside give a slower, food-and-market Cambodia after five days of temples.
because.nature: The Tonle Sap floating village at Kompong Phluk is a real fishing community on stilts, not a show.
because.culture: Angkor Wat, the Bayon faces, and Ta Prohm's tree roots are UNESCO-grade and worth the whole trip on their own.
because.exploration: Beng Mealea and Koh Ker are unrestored jungle temples reached by two hours of dirt road each way, with almost nobody else there.
